analysis: The only change in this PR is a new test in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift (head lines 189-229, theDaemonStateReportsTheFilterACommittedSwitchApplied). It runs a model switch against MockCoordinator with the commit either accepted or rejected. It then checks that the daemon state file reports enabled_models_at_start, and enabled_models_at_last_switch only after an accepted commit. It also checks that provider.toml holds new-model on accept and old-model after a rollback. This is test-only code. It adds no production attack surface, no change to the coordinator-provider protocol (TB-002), no change to attestation or authorization (TB-011), and no change to the prefix-cache storage covered by T-041. The test exercises the production paths it names (switchModels, writeDaemonState, ConfigManager), but those source changes are not in the supplied units. The state-file field enabled_models_at_last_switch and its writer sit in other files. They were not supplied, so the review could not check the production side. That side has two concerns: whether the state file is written owner-only and whether a stale or spoofed filter could mislead the status CLI. The cleanup in the test defers directory removal with try?, which is standard for tests. I identified no security regression in the supplied test file.
